text: Leveraging APEC 2026 outcomes,expanding cooperation towards APEC Vietnam 2027

Through activities at the APEC 2026 Leaders' Week and bilateral engagements in China, Vietnam continues to strengthen relations with partners, expand economic, trade, and scientific-technological cooperation, while laying the groundwork for hosting APEC 2027.

Politburo Member and Minister of Foreign Affairs Le Hoai Trung emphasized these outstanding results in an interview regarding General Secretary and President To Lam's participation in the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Leaders' Week and bilateral activities in China.
According to the Minister, the APEC 2026 Leaders' Week took place amidst profound global and regional economic transformations, presenting new opportunities and challenges.
The success of the conference was not only reflected in the documents and initiatives adopted but also in the economies' consensus on regional economic cooperation and integration directions.
For the first time in four years, the conference saw full attendance from senior leaders of all 21 member economies, reaffirming APEC's role in promoting dialogue, cooperation, and trust-building.
Leaders approved important documents on regional connectivity, digital economy, artificial intelligence, and the Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific, laying the foundation for new growth drivers.

Notably, the APEC Business Summit gathered over 2,000 delegates from hundreds of leading global and regional enterprises, focusing on innovation, digital transformation, green transition, human resource development, and supply chain connectivity.
Minister Le Hoai Trung stated that Vietnam participated in APEC 2026 as an active and proactive member, demonstrating the responsibility of an economy set to host APEC 2027.
Throughout 2026, Vietnam actively coordinated with China, proposed initiatives, participated in document drafting, and assumed chairing and coordinating roles in APEC cooperation mechanisms.
At the Leaders' Meeting, General Secretary and President To Lam was the first leader to speak at the discussion session and delivered a significant speech at the APEC Business Summit.

The General Secretary and President shared a vision of the era's transformations, APEC's development direction, and reaffirmed Vietnam's commitment, along with other members, to building a dynamic, cohesive, resilient, and prosperous Asia-Pacific region.
The speeches also highlighted achievements after 40 years of Doi Moi (Renovation), reform efforts, and breakthrough solutions to achieve Vietnam's development goals.

A key highlight was the official introduction of the APEC 2027 theme by the General Secretary and President: "Creating a New Era of Resilience, Innovation, and Shared Prosperity," along with three priorities: Enhancing productivity; Promoting regional trade and investment; Enhancing economic resilience, dynamism, and quality of life.
According to the Minister, the theme and priorities of APEC 2027 received support from APEC members, inheriting the Forum's long-term goals while addressing new development trends.

Through engagements with leaders of economies, international organizations, and the business community, Vietnam continues to strengthen political trust, deepen relations with partners, expand cooperation space for development, and garner support for the APEC 2027 agenda.
The participation of the Vietnamese business community also contributes to expanding opportunities for direct connection and cooperation between businesses and localities of member economies.
Assessing bilateral activities, Minister Le Hoai Trung noted that meetings with senior Chinese leaders and leaders of Guangdong and Yunnan provinces achieved many positive results.

A notable highlight was the combination of strengthening strategic orientation between the two Parties and countries with expanding substantive cooperation; simultaneously linking central planning with local implementation.
The most important highlight was the meeting between General Secretary and President To Lam and General Secretary and President of China Xi Jinping.
Both sides reaffirmed the special importance and long-term strategic significance of Vietnam-China relations; agreed on directions to elevate and deepen cooperation in the new phase.

Accordingly, both sides agreed to enhance political trust, maintain strategic exchanges, improve the quality of economic, trade, and investment cooperation; promote strategic infrastructure connectivity, science-technology, innovation, and cultural exchanges; while managing and appropriately addressing differences, maintaining a peaceful and stable environment.
Notably, both sides discussed directions to promote trade in a more balanced and healthy manner and enhance energy cooperation, in line with Vietnam's development needs.

At the local level, activities in Guangdong focused on leveraging cooperation potential with China's economic, industrial, science-technology, and innovation centers, especially the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area.

Both sides aim to promote high-quality investment, digital transformation, high-tech industry, production chain, and supply chain linkage, creating conditions for businesses to engage more deeply in high-value-added fields.

In Yunnan, the focus of cooperation is on transportation infrastructure connectivity, especially railways; improving customs clearance efficiency, developing border economy, logistics, trade, tourism, and people-to-people exchanges.

Forums connecting science-technology, innovation, and development strategies held in Shenzhen and Kunming also contributed to concretizing cooperation directions into programs and projects, aligned with the development needs of businesses and localities of both countries.
Alongside economic cooperation, youth and cultural exchanges continue to be emphasized to strengthen the social foundation of bilateral relations.

Minister Le Hoai Trung affirmed that the results of the mission continue to create new foundations and momentum for the Vietnam-China relations to develop stably, healthily, and sustainably, increasingly going deeper, contributing positively to the development of each country in the new phase.
